# gh-857: [GOAL] SM must CONCLUDE GitHub's required-check placeholders (in_progress, no-run-id, app=github-actions) when the head's real verdict is green — stamps don't override, FIFO burns the mutex on pinned oldest-approved PRs (fa #1457 live: 9 instances)

## Description

## Live

fa #1457 (dispatch-only CI PR) is green 9 times but unmergeable: GitHub mints in_progress "required-check placeholder" check-runs (app=github-actions, html_url with NO numeric run id) ~30s after a dispatch whose jobs haven't stamped yet. When the real job later stamps its own check-run (or the SM stamps a verdict via factory #510), the placeholder NEVER concludes and the required-check gate reads the placeholder's in_progress forever — mergeStateStatus BLOCKED, mergePullRequest rejects "Required status check X is in progress" (even --admin). SM stamps (later, completed/success) do NOT override it (live proof: #1457 fd1b9aa2 — placeholder 18:51:25 vs SM stamp 19:04:35, gate still BLOCKED). The oldest-approved FIFO then burns the serial mutex on such a PR every cycle (arm → full CI dispatch → green → gate pinned → sweep → re-arm; ~35 min wasted per hour) and operator parks (validation_failed) self-clear via gh-750 because the SM's green notion (dispatched-run verdicts) diverges from the gate's.

Evidence trail: gh-848 comments (9 instances on #1457 across 6 heads; merges succeed only when no placeholder exists — #1534 merged WITH late placeholders, so supersede paths exist but are unreliable).

## Goal

The SM must CONCLUDE placeholder check-runs. On any head where the SM has a real green verdict (dispatched run concluded success): for each required-context check-run that (a) has status in_progress/queued, (b) has html_url without a numeric run id (placeholder shape), and (c) has no live workflow run producing that context — PATCH it via checks:write to status=completed, conclusion=success (matching the real verdict; skipped if the real stamp is skipped), output referencing the covering run. Runs inside merge-validated's probe so a pinned green PR unblocks the SAME tick. If the Actions app's check-runs reject PATCH by the workflow token (ownership rules), fall back to the gh-852 auto-reset (fresh sha) as today — but log the 403 evidence to gh-848.

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR merges after one SM tick without operator action.
2. AC2: a placeholder with a LIVE run behind it is never concluded (fail-safe: probe hasActiveDispatchedRun).
3. AC3: red real verdicts never conclude placeholders green (verdict mirror only).

## References

gh-848 (placeholder law + 9 instances), gh-852/#853 (auto-reset — necessary but insufficient), gh-842 (zombie detector misses the placeholder shape), fa #1457.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

## PR Description

## gh-857: SM concludes required-check placeholders on green heads — in-place, same tick

### Root Cause
- Branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head): a pending link-less placeholder (no run id in `html_url`) pins `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` forever — later SM green stamps never override it (live fa #1457, 9 instances).
- The only engine cure was the gh-852 fresh-sha reset + full CI re-dispatch (~35 min/hour of FIFO mutex burn per pinned PR); the placeholder itself was never concluded.

### Fix
- `js/smAgent.js` — gh-857 in-place conclusion inside the gh-852 placeholder gate (`validate_pr`): when the head carries a real green verdict (`greenCoverRun` — newest completed-success dispatched run) and the whole-head rollup shows no active run (`hasActiveHeadRun`), PATCH each placeholder check-run `completed/success` via checks:write with output referencing the covering run (workflow-token swap, gh-848 belt pattern). On full success: no fresh-sha reset, no CI re-dispatch — the head unblocks the same tick (check-run-completed event → merge fast path).
- Fallback unchanged: a rejected PATCH (403 ownership) logs the evidence to the PR (gh-848 trail) and runs the gh-852 fresh-sha reset as today; no App token configured → reset directly.
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` — `placeholders()` now carries the check-run `id` (the PATCH target).

### Test Coverage
- `test_smAgent.js` gh-857: AC1 two placeholders PATCH-concluded in place (verdict-mirrored, covering run referenced, token swapped, no reset/dispatch) — PASSED; AC2 live run behind → never concluded — PASSED; AC3 no green verdict → never concluded green, reset fires — PASSED; 403 → evidence comment + gh-852 reset — PASSED.
- `test_checkRunZombies.js`: placeholder `id` passthrough — PASSED.
- Full suite: **2529 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes
- AC1's "same tick": the PATCH fires a check-run-completed webhook that drives the event-driven merge bot; the cron merge-validated rule consumes the unblocked head on the next tick at worst.
- The conclusion is a verdict mirror only (green covers conclude `success`); the per-PR reset cap is not consumed by in-place conclusions.

## Description

## Live

fa #1457 (dispatch-only CI PR) is green 9 times but unmergeable: GitHub mints in_progress "required-check placeholder" check-runs (app=github-actions, html_url with NO numeric run id) ~30s after a dispatch whose jobs haven't stamped yet. When the real job later stamps its own check-run (or the SM stamps a verdict via factory #510), the placeholder NEVER concludes and the required-check gate reads the placeholder's in_progress forever — mergeStateStatus BLOCKED, mergePullRequest rejects "Required status check X is in progress" (even --admin). SM stamps (later, completed/success) do NOT override it (live proof: #1457 fd1b9aa2 — placeholder 18:51:25 vs SM stamp 19:04:35, gate still BLOCKED). The oldest-approved FIFO then burns the serial mutex on such a PR every cycle (arm → full CI dispatch → green → gate pinned → sweep → re-arm; ~35 min wasted per hour) and operator parks (validation_failed) self-clear via gh-750 because the SM's green notion (dispatched-run verdicts) diverges from the gate's.

Evidence trail: gh-848 comments (9 instances on #1457 across 6 heads; merges succeed only when no placeholder exists — #1534 merged WITH late placeholders, so supersede paths exist but are unreliable).

## Goal

The SM must CONCLUDE placeholder check-runs. On any head where the SM has a real green verdict (dispatched run concluded success): for each required-context check-run that (a) has status in_progress/queued, (b) has html_url without a numeric run id (placeholder shape), and (c) has no live workflow run producing that context — PATCH it via checks:write to status=completed, conclusion=success (matching the real verdict; skipped if the real stamp is skipped), output referencing the covering run. Runs inside merge-validated's probe so a pinned green PR unblocks the SAME tick. If the Actions app's check-runs reject PATCH by the workflow token (ownership rules), fall back to the gh-852 auto-reset (fresh sha) as today — but log the 403 evidence to gh-848.

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR merges after one SM tick without operator action.
2. AC2: a placeholder with a LIVE run behind it is never concluded (fail-safe: probe hasActiveDispatchedRun).
3. AC3: red real verdicts never conclude placeholders green (verdict mirror only).

## References

gh-848 (placeholder law + 9 instances), gh-852/#853 (auto-reset — necessary but insufficient), gh-842 (zombie detector misses the placeholder shape), fa #1457.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

## PR Description

Closes #857
## gh-857: SM concludes required-check placeholders on green heads — in-place, same tick

### Root Cause
- Branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head): a pending link-less placeholder (no run id in `html_url`) pins `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` forever — later SM green stamps never override it (live fa #1457, 9 instances).
- The only engine cure was the gh-852 fresh-sha reset + full CI re-dispatch (~35 min/hour of FIFO mutex burn per pinned PR); the placeholder itself was never concluded.

### Fix
- `js/smAgent.js` — gh-857 in-place conclusion inside the gh-852 placeholder gate (`validate_pr`): when the head carries a real green verdict (`greenCoverRun` — newest completed-success dispatched run) and the whole-head rollup shows no active run (`hasActiveHeadRun`), PATCH each placeholder check-run `completed/success` via checks:write with output referencing the covering run (workflow-token swap, gh-848 belt pattern). On full success: no fresh-sha reset, no CI re-dispatch — the head unblocks the same tick (check-run-completed event → merge fast path).
- Fallback unchanged: a rejected PATCH (403 ownership) logs the evidence to the PR (gh-848 trail) and runs the gh-852 fresh-sha reset as today; no App token configured → reset directly.
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` — `placeholders()` now carries the check-run `id` (the PATCH target).

### Test Coverage
- `test_smAgent.js` gh-857: AC1 two placeholders PATCH-concluded in place (verdict-mirrored, covering run referenced, token swapped, no reset/dispatch) — PASSED; AC2 live run behind → never concluded — PASSED; AC3 no green verdict → never concluded green, reset fires — PASSED; 403 → evidence comment + gh-852 reset — PASSED.
- `test_checkRunZombies.js`: placeholder `id` passthrough — PASSED.
- Full suite: **2529 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes
- AC1's "same tick": the PATCH fires a check-run-completed webhook that drives the event-driven merge bot; the cron merge-validated rule consumes the unblocked head on the next tick at worst.
- The conclusion is a verdict mirror only (green covers conclude `success`); the per-PR reset cap is not consumed by in-place conclusions.

## Live

fa #1457 (dispatch-only CI PR) is green 9 times but unmergeable: GitHub mints in_progress "required-check placeholder" check-runs (app=github-actions, html_url with NO numeric run id) ~30s after a dispatch whose jobs haven't stamped yet. When the real job later stamps its own check-run (or the SM stamps a verdict via factory #510), the placeholder NEVER concludes and the required-check gate reads the placeholder's in_progress forever — mergeStateStatus BLOCKED, mergePullRequest rejects "Required status check X is in progress" (even --admin). SM stamps (later, completed/success) do NOT override it (live proof: #1457 fd1b9aa2 — placeholder 18:51:25 vs SM stamp 19:04:35, gate still BLOCKED). The oldest-approved FIFO then burns the serial mutex on such a PR every cycle (arm → full CI dispatch → green → gate pinned → sweep → re-arm; ~35 min wasted per hour) and operator parks (validation_failed) self-clear via gh-750 because the SM's green notion (dispatched-run verdicts) diverges from the gate's.

Evidence trail: gh-848 comments (9 instances on #1457 across 6 heads; merges succeed only when no placeholder exists — #1534 merged WITH late placeholders, so supersede paths exist but are unreliable).

## Goal

The SM must CONCLUDE placeholder check-runs. On any head where the SM has a real green verdict (dispatched run concluded success): for each required-context check-run that (a) has status in_progress/queued, (b) has html_url without a numeric run id (placeholder shape), and (c) has no live workflow run producing that context — PATCH it via checks:write to status=completed, conclusion=success (matching the real verdict; skipped if the real stamp is skipped), output referencing the covering run. Runs inside merge-validated's probe so a pinned green PR unblocks the SAME tick. If the Actions app's check-runs reject PATCH by the workflow token (ownership rules), fall back to the gh-852 auto-reset (fresh sha) as today — but log the 403 evidence to gh-848.

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR merges after one SM tick without operator action.
2. AC2: a placeholder with a LIVE run behind it is never concluded (fail-safe: probe hasActiveDispatchedRun).
3. AC3: red real verdicts never conclude placeholders green (verdict mirror only).

## References

gh-848 (placeholder law + 9 instances), gh-852/#853 (auto-reset — necessary but insufficient), gh-842 (zombie detector misses the placeholder shape), fa #1457.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

💡 **SUGGESTION: dedupe the 403 evidence comment — a persistently-rejected PATCH re-posts it every tick until the storm cap parks the reset**

When the Actions app refuses `checks:write` PATCH by the workflow token (the exact ownership scenario this fallback exists for, and a state that will not heal by itself), this block runs on **every tick**: PATCH → 403 → evidence comment → gh-852 reset → marker. Until `placeholderRetryAllowed` parks the reset (default cap 5 per 2h window), the PR accumulates up to ~5 identical 🔒 comments per window — and after the window/head change it starts over.

The codebase already has the dedupe pattern for exactly this audit-churn shape: `postGhostGuardAudit` + `validationLiveness.ghostGuardMarks` (one marker per (event, head), re-read from PR comments). Consider a `gh857EvidencePosted(prComments)`-style guard (or a marker substring like the `PLACEHOLDER_PARK_MARKER`) so the 403 evidence is logged once per head. Not blocking — the cap bounds the spam — but the gh-848 trail is easier to read with one entry per head.

💡 **SUGGESTION: in DRY mode the in-place conclusion never "completes", so a dry tick logs the conclusion AND falls through to the gh-852 reset path**

In `concludePlaceholderCheckRuns` the DRY branch logs the would-be PATCH but does not increment `out.concluded`, so the caller's `phConc.concluded === vPh.length` check is always false under DRY. A dry-run tick therefore prints the dry conclusion lines *and* continues into the fresh-sha reset path below (also dry-guarded), presenting a reset that a live tick would not perform.

Consider `if (DRY) { out.concluded++; ... return; }` so DRY mirrors the live control flow — consistent with how the reset path reports its dry state.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the head run rollup is fetched twice per candidate — reuse the dispatch-race guard's read**

~60 lines above, the gh-748 dispatch-race guard already calls `headWorkflowRunsSafe(effectiveRepoInfo, vHead0)` (line ~2288), and this block fetches the identical rollup again. The codebase comments elsewhere note the "fetch once and share it with the guard family" pattern (see the #695 note above `hasActiveHeadRun`). Hoisting one `vHeadRuns` variable for both guards saves one `gh api` round-trip per placeholder-pinned candidate per tick. Minor — the path is rare — but cheap to fix while the code is fresh.

💡 **SUGGESTION: missing test for the no-App-token skip (`silentToken` absent)**

AC1–AC3 and the 403 fallback are well covered, but the guard `(RUN_JOB_PARAMS || {}).silentToken` at the top of the in-place conclusion block has no test: with a green head, placeholders, and **no** `silentToken` in jobParams, the engine must skip the PATCH entirely and go straight to the gh-852 reset (the "with no App token configured the in-place cure is skipped entirely" branch in the block comment). A short variant of the AC1 test with `silentToken` omitted (asserting zero PATCH commands, reset fires) would pin that contract — it is the deployment-config difference between "cheap cure" and "full reset", i.e. the highest-cost branch boundary in the change.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Until `placeholderRetryAllowed` parks the reset (default cap 5 per 2h window), the PR accumulates up to ~5 identical 🔒 comments per window — and after the window/head change it starts over.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

Until `placeholderRetryAllowed` parks the reset (default cap 5 per 2h window), the PR accumulates up to ~5 identical 🔒 comments per window — and after the window/head change it starts over.

A dry-run tick therefore prints the dry conclusion lines *and* continues into the fresh-sha reset path below (also dry-guarded), presenting a reset that a live tick would not perform.

Consider `if (DRY) { out.concluded++; ... return; }` so DRY mirrors the live control flow — consistent with how the reset path reports its dry state.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

## Review Summary — PR #858 (gh-857)

**Verdict: APPROVE** — 0 blocking, 0 important, 4 suggestions.

### What was reviewed
The PR adds in-place conclusion of GitHub's required-check placeholders in `js/smAgent.js`: when a pinned head carries a real green verdict (newest completed-success dispatched run, `greenCoverRun`) and no active run on the head (`hasActiveHeadRun` fail-safe), each placeholder check-run is PATCHed `completed/success` via `checks:write` on the workflow token — avoiding the expensive gh-852 fresh-sha reset + full CI re-dispatch. On 403 rejection it logs evidence to the PR and falls back to the gh-852 reset. `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` now passes the check-run `id` through as the PATCH target.

### Verification
- Re-read the full changed files and surrounding `validate_pr` flow (green-cover void, latch-skip, gh-748 race guard, gh-852 placeholder gate, cap/pool-free logic)
- Confirmed AC1/AC2/AC3 semantics in code match the ticket; guards are fail-closed where required (`phHeadRuns !== null`, green-cover probe try/catch → null)
- Re-ran the full test suite locally via dmtools GraalJS: **2529 passed, 0 failed** — matching the PR claim
- Checked AGENTS.md conventions: new code uses `var`/plain functions, dmtools globals, hoisted requires — compliant

### Suggestions raised (inline)
1. **403 evidence comment dedupe** — a persistently-rejected PATCH re-posts the 🔒 comment every tick until the storm cap parks the reset; the `postGhostGuardAudit` marker pattern exists for exactly this
2. **DRY mode never completes the conclusion** — `out.concluded` isn't incremented in the DRY branch, so dry ticks also walk the reset path
3. **Duplicate head-run rollup fetch** — gh-748 race guard and the gh-857 block each call `headWorkflowRunsSafe` for the same head; hoist one shared read
4. **Missing test for the no-`silentToken` skip** — the highest-cost branch boundary (cheap cure vs. full reset) is unpinned
